summary.text: Trent Kelly is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Mississippi's 1st District, elected in a 2015 special election. A Mississippi attorney and former district attorney, he served 39 years in the Mississippi Army National Guard, retiring as a Major General in April 2025. He sits on the Agriculture, Intelligence and Armed Services committees.

paragraphs.text: Kelly was born March 1, 1966, in Union, Mississippi, and graduated from Union High School and East Central Community College.
He earned a bachelor's degree and a law degree from the University of Mississippi and, in 2010, a master's degree in Strategic Studies from the U.S. Army War College.

Kelly began serving in the Mississippi Army National Guard as a combat engineer in 1985. He mobilized for Desert Storm in 1990, deployed to Iraq in 2005 and again in 2009-2010 as a battalion commander, and retired as a Major General in April 2025 after 39 years of service. His decorations include two Bronze Stars and the Combat Action Badge.
Before Congress, Kelly worked as a department store manager and in private law practice in Saltillo, and he served as Tupelo city prosecutor from 1999 to 2011.
He was district attorney for Mississippi's 1st Judicial District from 2012 to 2015, handling felony cases in seven north Mississippi counties.
He won the 2015 special election to succeed Rep. Alan Nunnelee, taking 70% of the vote against Democrat Walter Zinn in the June 2, 2015 runoff.
In the 119th Congress Kelly sits on the Agriculture, Intelligence (Permanent Select) and Armed Services committees, and he chairs the Armed Services Subcommittee on Seapower and Projection Forces.
He was unopposed in the March 10, 2026 Republican primary.
According to his congressional website, he lives in Saltillo with his wife, Sheila, and their three children, and is a member of Saltillo First United Methodist Church.
